name: Primary Bone Dysplasia with Progressive Ossification of Skin, Skeletal Muscle, Fascia, Tendons and Ligaments

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva

criteria.description: Congenital malformation of the great toes (hallux valgus or shortened first metatarsal)
Progressive heterotopic ossification in characteristic anatomic patterns involving skeletal muscle, fascia, tendons, and ligaments
Episodes of painful soft tissue swellings (flare-ups) preceding ossification

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital great toe malformation plus progressive heterotopic ossification in typical anatomical locations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for ACVR1 mutations can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital malformation of the great toes
pathognomonic.notes: Hallux valgus or shortened first metatarsal present at birth
searchTerms: abnormal big toe shape present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive heterotopic ossification of soft tissues
pathognomonic.notes: Ectopic bone formation in muscles, fascia, tendons, and ligaments
searchTerms: gradual abnormal bone growth in soft tissue
bone forming in muscles and skin

common.symptomName: Restricted joint mobility due to ossification
common.notes: Progressive limitation of movement in affected joints
searchTerms: joint movement limited by bone growth
stiff joints due to abnormal ossification
bone shape changes from abnormal bone formation
bone malformations due to extra bone growth

common.notes: Due to progressive ossification and joint stiffness

occasional.symptomName: Hearing loss due to ossification of middle ear structures
searchTerms: hearing loss from middle ear bone hardening
middle ear bone stiffening hearing loss

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory restriction from thoracic cage ossification
searchTerms: breathing restriction from chest bone hardening
thoracic cage ossification causing respiratory issues
limited lung expansion due to chest bone changes

occasional.notes: Due to replacement of muscle tissue by bone
searchTerms: reduced muscle strength due to ossification
weak muscles related to bone changes

rare.symptomName: Neuropathic pain due to nerve entrapment

rare.notes: Reduced bone density in non-ossified skeletal regions
searchTerms: low bone density in normal bones

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during flare-ups (e.g., ESR, CRP)
imaging: Radiographs showing heterotopic ossification in characteristic anatomical patterns
CT and MRI demonstrating soft tissue ossification and flare-ups
genetic: Heterozygous mutation in ACVR1 gene (most commonly R206H mutation)
other: Physical exam revealing congenital great toe malformations

distinguishingFeatures: Heterotopic ossification begins in dermis and subcutaneous fat
Autosomal dominant inheritance with GNAS mutations
Non-progressive and limited to injury site

redFlags: Rapidly progressive joint ankylosis leading to immobility
Flare-ups triggered by intramuscular injections or trauma
Respiratory compromise due to thoracic cage ossification
references: Kaplan FS, Shore EM. Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva: A Rare Genetic Disorder of Extra-skeletal Bone Formation. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2008.
Shore EM, Xu M, Feldman GJ, et al. A recurrent mutation in the BMP type I receptor ACVR1 causes fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva. Nat Genet. 2006.
